decided.question: what a client principal receives from the staff routes that resolve their caller from Membership in their own service, which carry no CapabilityGuard and so cannot answer the fixed forbidden body
decided.chose: 403 {"message":"Forbidden","statusCode":403} from those routes, the refusal they already make; TC-02-INT-08 now names the guard-gated routes and the service-gated routes separately and asserts the matching body for each
decided.rejected: teaching those routes the guard's fixed body or a message of this spec's own
decided.why: rule 1 — the spec had taken no position on the body of those routes, and the code already refuses a caller with no active Membership with that body; a new named message on every staff surface would also let a client principal tell one surface from another
decided.recordedAt: requirement 14a, and the Expected Result of TC-02-INT-08
decided.verifiedBy: grep -rln "RequireCapability" apps/api/src --include=*.controller.ts -> documents/autofill, documents/document-templates, documents/envelopes, mail/outbox, organizations/signing-settings, requests/requests only; members/projects/time-tracking/vacation/clients controllers carry @UseGuards(SessionGuard, OrgScopeGuard); their requireCaller throws `new ForbiddenException()`, and node_modules/@nestjs/common/exceptions/http.exception.js createBody returns { message: 'Forbidden', statusCode: 403 } for an empty argument

decided.question: what a client principal sees when they type the URL of a staff screen
decided.chose: the shell sends a client principal who opens any /org/{orgId}/... route other than the two requests routes to /org/{orgId}/requests, and draws no staff screen
decided.rejected: a forbidden state drawn on the staff screen
decided.why: rule 4 — the redirect uses screens and a principalKind this spec already defines and needs no new empty state, data-testid or message, where a shared forbidden state would be a new artefact on every staff screen and could not be taken back cheaply
decided.recordedAt: requirement 14b, edge case 8, and the last step and expected result of TC-02-E2E-01

decided.question: how the People section's gating is observed for a role that cannot reach the client detail at all
decided.chose: drop the `user` half of TC-02-E2E-05 and observe the rule at integration, in TC-02-INT-19, which calls GET .../clients/{clientId}/users as a `user` and asserts 403 manageForbidden
decided.rejected: keeping the E2E assertion that the People section and the invite control are absent for a `user`
decided.why: rule 3 — the E2E assertion cannot fail: a `user` is answered 404 by the client detail before any People markup exists, so it passes whether or not the section is gated; the integration observation can fail

decided.question: how the pending invitation row on the People section is addressed, given a pending invitation carries no id in the payload

decided.question: whether a clients-scoped route may answer a named 403 where the existing clients routes collapse a missing capability to 404 so the resource is not revealed
decided.chose: the three client-user routes answer 403 manageForbidden, and the capability is checked before the client or the client membership named in the URL is read, so the refusal is identical for an id that exists and one that does not
decided.rejected: collapsing these three routes to 404 as the other clients-scoped routes do
decided.why: rule 3 — with the capability checked before the lookup, the 403 reveals nothing about what exists, so the safe answer and the named message are both available; collapsing to 404 would make manageForbidden unreachable
decided.recordedAt: requirement 9a, second paragraph, and the Errors line of the People list and remove contracts
